$schema: M3E Cursor design tokens. Units: points (pt) on a 32 x 32 pt cursor canvas.

primary30.role: Detail lines inside the body (finger separators)

onPrimaryContainer.role: Badge glyphs, loading-indicator active shape, outer hairline

tertiaryContainer.role: Expressive accent: shape badges, cursor centres (M3 baseline tertiary-90)

onTertiaryContainer.role: Glyphs on tertiary shapes (M3 baseline tertiary-10)

rim.role: Inner edge that separates the cursor from dark backgrounds

hairline.role: Outer edge that separates the rim from light backgrounds

rimWidth.role: White rim drawn outside every silhouette

hairlineWidth.role: Dark hairline drawn outside the rim

strokeWeight.role: Shafts of resize / move arrows, I-beam stem

badgeCorner.role: FAB corner radius (M3 FAB 16/56 ratio, rounded up)

badgeShapeSize.role: Width of a Material Shape badge (organic shapes need a little more than the 12 pt FAB)

badgeTone.role: Badge colour role: tertiary (expressive accent) or primary (container)

windows.role: Sizes inside each .cur / .ani frame; Windows picks one by cursor size and display scale

linux.role: Xcursor nominal size -> image size. The 32 pt canvas carries a margin, so a 24 px cursor uses a 32 px image to match Breeze-sized arrows

springSpatial.role: M3E expressive default spatial spring (scale, position)

springEffects.role: M3E default effects spring (morphs, no overshoot)

springMorph.role: Shape and glyph morphs: slow spatial speed, no overshoot, so a morph spans about four 100 ms frames
